mechanism_narrative: The Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) level is inversely related to S&P 500 returns: lower rates consistently predict positive 20-day forward returns, regardless of the absolute rate level.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% in a single month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The joint rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a monetary tightening cycle: when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.3% and FEDFUNDS monthly change exceeds 0.1%, S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days are negative.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.3% AND FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.1%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when both CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.1%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by UNRATE above 5% and rising by more than 0.1% monthly), S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days are negative due to slowing economic growth and rising unemployment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 5% and UNRATE monthly change > 0.1%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 500 thousand units, it signals a weakening housing market and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 500, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The level of industrial production (INDPRO) is inversely related to S&P 500 returns: lower industrial output consistently predicts positive 20-day forward returns, regardless of the absolute level of industrial production.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is below 90, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a demand-driven expansion regime (defined by rising GDP growth and rising RSAFS), S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days are positive due to strong consumer and business spending.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly change > 1.0% AND RSAFS monthly change > 0.5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when both GDPC1 quarterly change > 1.0% and RSAFS monthly change > 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% in a single month, it signals a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4% in a single month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
